content:
iPhone 18 Pro is about to debut, and with a major overhaul of this year's product lineup, it will become Apple's new standard model like never before.

Since there won't be a base iPhone 18, the iPhone 18 Pro will become Apple's default new device for this year.

Apple has launched multiple new iPhones every year for many years, and will undoubtedly continue to do so for years to come.

However, at Apple's event this week, the iPhone lineup will undergo a major overhaul.

Apple will not release the base 'iPhone' and 'iPhone Pro' versions as usual this year; the base iPhone 18 will be nowhere to be seen.

Multiple reports indicate that Apple will delay the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 until early 2027, leaving only the following models in the fall lineup:

By pushing the iPhone 18 back beyond its usual release window, the iPhone 18 Pro will essentially become Apple's new standard model.

Users who want a more affordable device can still choose last year's iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, or iPhone Air. However, throughout this fall and holiday season, none of Apple and its carrier partners' marketing will feature a flagship 'iPhone 18' as the new standard device; instead, the iPhone 18 Pro will take on that role.

The iPhone Ultra will be priced too high and the market is likely to remain relatively niche.

Therefore, for the average consumer looking to buy a 'new iPhone,' Apple will essentially offer only two choices: the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max.

It's an interesting experiment, and the iPhone 18 Pro may even become the best-selling new-generation Pro model; but combined with expected price increases, it also poses a risk for Apple. With no iPhone 18 available for upgrades in the market, potential upgraders may hold onto their existing iPhones even longer.

In any case, we'll soon find out whether Apple's new arrangement will work.

What are your thoughts on Apple's iPhone lineup changes this year? Let us know in the comments.
